scenario: Alterion 后端面试，面试官问「不那么时间敏感的活儿你怎么处理？」你说成了「decouple with some queue to debug, decouple, and don't interrupt the flow」，卡住了。
scenario_en: In an Alterion backend interview the interviewer asks how you handle work that isn't time-sensitive. You said "decouple with some queue to debug, decouple, and don't interrupt the flow" and stalled.
q: 想说「把不紧急的活儿丢队列里异步处理，不阻塞主请求」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "push non-urgent work onto a queue and handle it async so it doesn't block the request" — which line lands?
options: For the service that's not time-sensitive, I would decouple with some queue to debug, decouple, and not interrupt the flow.
So, so for the, for the work that can wait, we kind of, you know, put it somewhere else so it doesn't block the thing that...
For anything not time-sensitive, we drop it on a queue and process it async, so the request path stays fast.
Non-time-sensitive services shall be decoupled via a message queue to achieve asynchronous processing.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 卡壳复读：「drop it on a queue, process it async」一句说清机制；她原话把关键词摆错还打转，暴露没消化。
why: 不紧急的活儿入队再异步处理，一句带出「主路径解耦」。她的原话术语摆错位、还重复，听着像没想清楚。
why_en: Say "we drop it on a queue and process it async so the request path stays fast" — that names the mechanism in one clean line.
whenOtherWins: 若这活儿必须立刻返回、用户在等，就别异步，同步做完再回；此时入队反而是错的设计。
options_en: For the service that's not time-sensitive, I would decouple with some queue to debug, decouple, and not interrupt the flow.
So, so for the, for the work that can wait, we kind of, you know, put it somewhere else so it doesn't block the thing that...
For anything not time-sensitive, we drop it on a queue and process it async, so the request path stays fast.
Non-time-sensitive services shall be decoupled via a message queue to achieve asynchronous processing.
optionMeanings: 她的原话：术语摆错位、还打结重复。
「so so for the for the」一路打转。
一句把「入队 + 异步」的机制说清。
「shall be decoupled via」的念稿书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Her actual line: "decouple" misused as a verb, then repeated.
Loops on "so so for the for the," never names the mechanism.
"Drop it on a queue, process it async" — mechanism in one line.
A written-register "shall be decoupled via" recital.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻懂：请求不被拖慢。
像背文档，不像会怎么做。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you forcing keywords, not a real design.
They wait and still hear no "queue" or "async" anchor.
They instantly get it: decoupled path, request stays fast.
Sounds recited from a doc, not like how you'd build it.
optionDirectness: 错在词摆错、重复，机制没落地。
错在打转，队列异步没出口。
抓住入队→异步→主请求不拖慢。
错在语域，书面体口语显僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: keyword misplaced and repeated, mechanism never lands.
Wrong: pure looping, never says "queue" or "async" at all.
Nails the chain: drop on a queue, process async, fast request.
Wrong register — written style feels stiff spoken.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个缓冲区，请求先写进去，后台消费者慢慢取出处理，从而解耦生产和消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message queue is a buffer where work is enqueued and background workers pull it off to process later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不在原请求里等结果，把活儿丢到后台处理，主请求先返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Async means the work runs in the background instead of blocking the original request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户请求进来到返回响应走的那条主链路；异步就是把慢活儿从这条路上挪走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The request path is the main flow from an incoming request to its response; async moves slow work off it.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官追问：生产者发消息太快、消费者跟不上，你怎么办？你想表达「消费者反压、让生产者降速」，但一时不知道 backpressure 怎么说出口。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks: the producer outpaces the consumer — what do you do? You want to say "the consumer applies backpressure so the producer slows down" but blank on the term.
q: 想说「消费者跟不上时，用反压让生产者降速」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "when the consumer can't keep up, it uses backpressure to slow the producer" — which line is how an engineer says it?
options: When the consumer can't keep up, it pushes backpressure and the producer throttles down.
When the consumer is too slow, we do a back-pressing thing so the producer will send less.
so the, the consumer is slow, so the producer has to, to wait, to slow, to not send too much...
The consumer exerts backpressure upon the producer so as to regulate the ingestion rate.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 造词/打转：「pushes backpressure, producer throttles down」一句到位；「back-pressing」是造出来的错词，显得只听过没用过。
why: 反压名词形是 backpressure，动词搭 push/apply，配 producer throttles down。造词或打转都会露怯。
why_en: The consumer pushes backpressure and the producer throttles down — that's the exact collocation engineers use.
whenOtherWins: 若能靠丢消息或加缓冲扛短时高峰，就说 we buffer / drop and retry，不必谈反压；反压是针对持续过载。
options_en: When the consumer can't keep up, it pushes backpressure and the producer throttles down.
When the consumer is too slow, we do a back-pressing thing so the producer will send less.
so the, the consumer is slow, so the producer has to, to wait, to slow, to not send too much...
The consumer exerts backpressure upon the producer so as to regulate the ingestion rate.
optionMeanings: push backpressure + throttle down 标准搭配。
optionMeanings_en: The standard collocation: push backpressure, throttle down.
Loops on "so the the," never says backpressure.
A stiff "exerts backpressure upon" bureaucratic register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 一听造词，觉得你没用过。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer sees you've actually done flow control.
The coined term signals you've only read it, not used it.
They tune out before the key mechanism word arrives.
Over-formal — sounds like reading a paper, not designing.
optionDirectness: 错在术语形：back-pressing 不是词。
错在打转，反压始终没出口。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong term form — "back-pressing" isn't a word.
Wrong: looping, the word backpressure never comes out.
Wrong register — bureaucratic style feels stiff spoken.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游消费者跟不上时向上游发出的「慢点」信号，让生产者降速，避免堆爆。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backpressure is a signal a slow consumer sends upstream so the producer slows down instead of overflowing.

termDefinitions.meaning: producer 往队列写消息，consumer 从队列取消息处理；两端速率不匹配就要限流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A producer writes messages to the queue and a consumer pulls them off to process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动限制发送/处理速率；throttle down 就是降速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To throttle is to cap the rate; "throttle down" means slow the sending rate.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问：消费者进程崩了重启，怎么保证不丢不重乱？你想说「处理完再提交 offset，崩了从上次 offset 重放」，但 offset 这个词卡住了。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks: if the consumer crashes and restarts, how do you avoid losing or garbling messages? You want to say "commit the offset after processing and replay from the last committed offset" but stall on the term.
q: 想说「处理完才提交 offset，崩溃后从上次 offset 重放」，哪句最工程师？
q_en: You want to say "commit the offset only after processing, and on a crash replay from the last committed offset" — which line is most engineer-like?
options: We save the position number after we're done, so if it crashes we start from the last position we saved.
so we, we remember where we are, the, the number, so when it restart, we go back to where we were...
The offset is committed post-processing to enable resumption of the consumer upon failure.
We commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset.
tradeoff: 术语落地 vs 绕圈直译：「commit the offset after processing」一句闭环；「save the position number」绕开了 offset 和重放语义。
why: 读取位置叫 offset，搭 commit / resume from。处理后才提交＝at-least-once，崩了重放，业务要幂等。
why_en: Commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset and replays — that's at-least-once.
whenOtherWins: 若消息可丢、追求最低延迟，可先提交再处理（at-most-once），说 commit first, then process；此时不谈重放。
options_en: We save the position number after we're done, so if it crashes we start from the last position we saved.
so we, we remember where we are, the, the number, so when it restart, we go back to where we were...
The offset is committed post-processing to enable resumption of the consumer upon failure.
We commit the offset only after processing, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset.
optionMeanings: 「so we we the the number」绕圈。
提交 offset 与重放位置一句闭环。
optionMeanings_en: Uses "position number," dodging the term offset.
Loops on "so we we remember the the number."
A passive "is committed post-processing" written register.
Closes the loop: commit offset, resume from last committed.
optionScenarioImpacts: 懂你意思，但觉得没掌握标准词。
听不出你到底提不提交。
确认你懂提交时机与重放。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They follow you but sense you lack the standard term.
They can't tell if you commit, or replay, at all.
Reads like a spec, missing the "here's what I'd do" feel.
The interviewer sees you know commit timing and replay.
optionDirectness: 错在直译绕词，语义都糊了。
错在绕圈，提交时机没说清。
错在语域，被动书面显僵。
抓住提交时机与崩溃后从原位重放。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: paraphrase dodges "offset" and blurs replay.
Wrong: circling, commit timing never gets stated.
Wrong register — passive written style feels stiff.
Nails offset commit timing, then replay from last offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在分区里读到的位置编号；提交 offset 就是记录「我处理到这儿了」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position a consumer has read to in a partition; committing it records how far you've processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把当前读取位置持久化；处理完再提交，崩溃后就从这个点重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To commit the offset is to persist your read position so a restart resumes from that point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理后才提交 → 崩溃会重放未提交的消息，可能重复，所以业务要幂等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Committing after processing means a crash replays uncommitted messages at least once, so handling must be idempotent.

scenario: Alterion 面试，你想说「发到 topic，每个订阅者各拿一份」，结果说成「we put it in the Kafka Q, everyone who listen can get it」，把 pub/sub 扇出说成了点对点队列。
scenario_en: In an Alterion interview you want to say "publish to a topic and each subscriber gets its own copy," but you said "we put it in the Kafka Q, everyone who listen can get it," collapsing pub/sub fan-out into a point-to-point queue.
q: 想说「发布到 topic，扇出给每个订阅者各一份」，哪句最准？
q_en: You want to say "publish to a topic and fan out a copy to each subscriber" — which line is most precise?
options: We put it in the Kafka Q, and then everyone who listen can get the message from there.
We publish to a topic and fan out to each subscriber — every one gets its own copy.
The message is published to a topic and fanned out to all subscribing consumers respectively.
so we, we send it to the, the topic thing, and then the ones who want it, they each, they get...
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 混淆模型：「publish to a topic, fan out, each gets a copy」区分了 pub/sub 与点对点；她的「Kafka Q」把两种模型糊在一起。
why: pub/sub 是 publish to a topic + fan out，每个订阅者各一份；点对点队列一条消息只被一个消费者取走。说成「Kafka Q」会让人以为你不分这两种。
why_en: We publish to a topic and fan out a copy to each subscriber — that's pub/sub, not a point-to-point queue where one consumer takes each message.
whenOtherWins: 若每条消息只该被一个 worker 处理一次（任务分发），那是点对点队列，说 each message goes to one worker，别用扇出。
options_en: We put it in the Kafka Q, and then everyone who listen can get the message from there.
We publish to a topic and fan out to each subscriber — every one gets its own copy.
The message is published to a topic and fanned out to all subscribing consumers respectively.
so we, we send it to the, the topic thing, and then the ones who want it, they each, they get...
optionMeanings: 她的原话：说成「Kafka Q」，混淆两种模型。
optionMeanings_en: Her line: says "Kafka Q," blurring fan-out with point-to-point.
"Publish to a topic, fan out, each gets a copy" — precise.
A stiff "fanned out ... respectively" written register.
Loops on "the topic thing ... they each they get."
optionScenarioImpacts: 以为你分不清 pub/sub 和队列。
确认你懂扇出：各拿独立一份。
听不出是扇出还是抢占。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer thinks you can't tell pub/sub from a queue.
They confirm you get fan-out: each subscriber its own copy.
Reads like a doc, missing conversational feel.
They can't tell if it's fan-out or competing consumers.
optionDirectness: 错在模型混淆，扇出说成点对点。
错在打转，扇出关键点没落地。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: conflates fan-out with a point-to-point queue.
Nails pub/sub: publish to topic, fan out, each a copy.
Wrong: circling, the fan-out point never lands.

termDefinitions.meaning: pub/sub 里的消息类别通道；生产者发布到 topic，订阅者按 topic 收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A topic is a named channel in pub/sub; producers publish to it and subscribers receive from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条消息复制分发给多个接收方，每个订阅者各拿一份独立副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one message is copied out to many receivers, each subscriber getting its own copy.

termDefinitions.meaning: pub/sub 一条消息扇出给所有订阅者；点对点队列一条消息只被一个消费者取走。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In pub/sub one message fans out to all subscribers; in a point-to-point queue one consumer takes each message.
